screening_boundary: Eligibility only. No source verifier, reference solution, gold outcome, published model result, or archived trajectory was consulted. No final optimum was computed. Ordinary methods are proposed and may require practical validation.
solver_boundary: Only independently parsed literal or deliberately bounded witness representations, never direct evaluation of corpus-provided executable text. Validate full original feasibility before claiming a result.

rows.witness_format: A finite circular list of colors of the disclosed length, with fixed alphabet.
rows.local_conflict: An invalid color or a fully instantiated cyclic window missing a required color refutes that construction.
rows.ordinary_complete: Try residue-periodic coloring, then use an exact cyclic sliding-window counter as the feasibility certificate. Exhaustive cyclic-state search with rotation symmetry is an exact fallback for fixed-length feasibility only.
rows.qualification: The query's extremal relation is textually incomplete. The output instruction fixes both the alphabet parameter and necklace length, and asks feasibility instead of the original largest impossible length.

rows.witness_format: Integer segment endpoints and an ordered partition of segment IDs into rows.
rows.local_conflict: An out-of-range or repeated segment, a completed row of incorrect length, or an assigned segment whose start residue disagrees with its left-to-right row placement gives an exact conflict.
rows.ordinary_complete: Derive row phase from the endpoint residue constraint, then optimize over feasible residue-state tilings with a structural lower bound. An interval-choice CP-SAT or MILP on the derived states is a complete finite baseline if executed to an optimality certificate.
rows.qualification: Optimize the scaled original construction objective with its endpoint convention and prohibition on reversals. No target value was provided or inferred during screening.

rows.witness_format: A binary rook occupancy matrix on the fixed board.
rows.local_conflict: A rook whose deletion leaves the union of occupied rows and columns unchanged violates the original all-rooks-essential property.
rows.ordinary_complete: Use the row-column incidence graph. Every edge must touch a degree-one endpoint, so nonempty components are stars. Count such components and construct a matching-bound board, then verify every deletion from the original predicate.
rows.qualification: A currently exclusive line-of-sight attack can cease to be exclusive after deleting a blocker. Recompute original danger coverage after each deletion and avoid substituting the pre-deletion output hint. Keep only one case from the star-forest family.

rows.witness_format: An ordered list of distinct squares on a fixed board.
rows.local_conflict: A repeated or out-of-range vertex, or a purported move without row/column alignment, refutes a path. A noncrossing move refutes only the instruction's strengthened path restriction.
rows.ordinary_complete: Construct a graph with both crossing and noncrossing aligned edges and maximize crossing edge count over vertex-simple paths by exact branch-and-bound or integer programming. Solve the all-crossing induced restriction separately.
rows.qualification: The original optimizes the number of crossing moves while allowing general rook moves. The instruction forbids all noncrossing moves. No proof of equal optima was available in the permitted fields.

rows.witness_format: A fixed ternary board of blank or two colors.
rows.local_conflict: For one colored square, more than five already committed opposite-color cells in its row and column is a prefix-stable conflict. A smaller count is invalid only when both relevant lines are complete or the remaining potential is insufficient.
rows.ordinary_complete: Aggregate row and column color-count types, derive which typed intersections can be colored, and certify a structural upper bound with a realizing board. Use symmetry-reduced CP-SAT or MILP with exact row/column totals and a proven optimality gap of zero when tractable.
rows.qualification: The row-column intersection is the subject's own cell and cannot count as opposite color twice. Full validation should use exact counts rather than a floating relaxation.

rows.witness_format: A fixed-length sequence of fully typed morning snow moves.
rows.local_conflict: An out-of-domain move or a wrong claimed cell state after a completed prefix can be rejected by deterministic integer replay, including the night increment in its original order.
rows.ordinary_complete: Use an exact deterministic replay checker and structural snow-mass and grid-boundary bounds. A bounded state-space search or exact integer optimization with move and state variables is complete for the stated horizon if solved to optimality.
rows.qualification: Replay is a strong feasibility and score baseline for any schedule. It does not certify minimum achievable maximum on its own.

rows.witness_format: A fixed-size square permutation matrix of ranks.
rows.local_conflict: A duplicate or out-of-range rank refutes feasibility. Four already instantiated rectangle corners can refute a claimed counted rectangle by exact comparison of its two lowest ranks.
rows.ordinary_complete: Derive a bound by row-pair order statistics and construct a permutation attaining the bound, or use exact order-variable CP-SAT or MILP with reified rectangle predicates, structural bounds, and symmetry.
rows.qualification: A false named rectangle contribution invalidates that contribution only. The rest of the matrix may still be a feasible construction.

rows.witness_format: A finite binary board avoiding the forbidden three-corner pattern.
rows.local_conflict: Three selected corners with shared row and column refute the avoidance witness. In the incidence graph this occurs exactly when a selected edge has two endpoints of degree at least two.
rows.ordinary_complete: Count and construct bipartite star forests and verify the forbidden-pattern bound. For an integer cardinality forcing threshold, translate the optimal avoider count plus one with its domain assumptions.
rows.qualification: The original forcing statement and its avoider dual are tractable, but this repeats the essential row-column star-forest structure of the smaller accepted CB-78. Excluded from the primary family shortlist for diversity.

rows.witness_format: A fixed box-by-slot matrix of color IDs or an equivalent incidence representation.
rows.local_conflict: A box with a repeated color, or two completed box incidences sharing two distinct colors, violates the original color-pair restrictions.
rows.ordinary_complete: Double-count color incidences and box-pair intersections to bound the palette, then construct a block packing. A complete exact baseline is CP-SAT over canonicalized color labels and pair intersections with proven optimality.
rows.qualification: Reject only once an actual pair collision or duplicate is present. Use full distinct-color and original box cardinality checks at delivery.

rows.witness_format: A nonempty set of axis-spanning brick placements specified by opposite-face endpoints.
rows.local_conflict: A malformed placement or overlapping interiors refutes feasibility. A nonboundary long face without any admissible support refutes a completed construction, or a partial construction only after all remaining support placements are ruled out.
rows.ordinary_complete: Enumerate axis-line placements and encode nonempty selection, cell exclusivity, and disjunctive face support exactly in CP-SAT or MILP. Use cube symmetries, prove a lower bound, and independently replay the optimal placement.
rows.qualification: The checker must require overlap with a long face's relative interior. Do not silently replace that condition by complete face coverage or accept an empty selection.

rows.witness_format: A fixed-length list of distinct nonnegative integer coordinate pairs with no stated coordinate bound.
rows.local_conflict: An out-of-domain or repeated point refutes feasibility. A claimed counted edge is refuted by its exact absolute determinant differing from one.
rows.ordinary_complete: Prove a graph bound using primitive-ray slope order and an outerplanar/Farey-type noncrossing argument, then exhibit and verify a fan construction. Any finite coordinate search needs an independently justified bound before it can certify global optimality.
rows.qualification: The witness has finitely many integer entries even though the domain is unbounded. The structural approach is proposed, with no optimum or proof admitted during screening.

rows.witness_format: A fixed finite binary selection of squares containing placements of every required template.
rows.local_conflict: A proposed occurrence can be refuted by one absent required square. Global absence for a template requires ruling out every legal placement.
rows.ordinary_complete: Use bitset or template correlation across legal translations and orientations, followed by exact set-cover or integer optimization for the fixed instance where needed.
rows.qualification: The output instruction discloses a concrete size and selected-square cap. It changes the original asymptotic exponent objective into fixed-instance feasibility and is suitable only as a distinctly named control.

rows.witness_format: A finite grid of stick IDs, each inducing one straight contiguous set of cells.
rows.local_conflict: A bent label or two proven common unit edges between the same two sticks refutes feasibility. Disconnected cells are a conflict only when connecting them is impossible or the assignment is complete.
rows.ordinary_complete: Enumerate every admissible straight stick and solve an exact cover with pairwise incompatibility for excessive shared edges, optimizing selected stick count and supplying an independent lower bound where possible.
rows.qualification: A grammar-based validator should derive stick geometry from the delivered matrix rather than trust separately reported counts.
